<a id="mission"></a>

## Mission

Cross-model review of plan 006-worktree-diff after composition, before the PR into main. The plan's claim: a worktree of a registered repo becomes searchable without a manual add, costs nothing for content identical to the main tree, resolves to the asking checkout's version, and unreferences cleanly when removed. Phase 1 MEASURED all four behaviours before anything was built — assets/probe-report.md is the evidence contract, and the phase-2 units were ruled from it. Your job is to judge whether the built thing matches BOTH the plan and that measured evidence, and whether the two units compose without a seam defect. You are read-only.

<a id="instructions"></a>

## Instructions

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| i1 | Orient: read the plan (rendered .dd.md), the impl-guide (the intended decomposition + interfaces), and then the full diff of the branch against its base. DOGFOOD FLOWSPACE: use `flowspace3 search` to locate consumers/related code by meaning while reviewing; report misses as friction. |
| i2 | Review with the /builder review discipline: verify claims against fresh evidence — run targeted tests yourself, read exit status, never trust a green claim you did not see. |
| i3 | Priority order: (1) plan promises that are not actually true, (2) composition-seam defects between units, (3) interface drift from the impl-guide, (4) correctness/safety in the changed code, (5) test gaps on the contract. Style noise is unwanted. |
| i4 | Findings: at most the material ones, each with severity (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM), exact location, the claim, the proof, and the smallest fix. `no_material_findings` is a valid verdict. |
| i5 | Deliver as a ddoc review record in the plan folder (assets/reviews/), build it, and send the PM the path + a one-line verdict. |
| i6 | READ THE PROBE REPORT FIRST (docs/plans/006-worktree-diff/assets/probe-report.md). It is unusual and it is the point of this plan: every phase-2 unit exists to close a MEASURED gap, and each unit's done bar is a predicate flip in the harness's own receipt.env — p1_auto_discovered 0-&gt;1, p4_root_still_registered 1-&gt;0, p3_search_context_sensitive 0-&gt;1, p3_wrong_version_leak_to_main 1-&gt;0, with p3_get_context_sensitive and p4_served_after_gc unchanged. Verify those flips against a RUN, not against a claim in a done report. |
| i7 | THE FOUR HIGHEST-VALUE QUESTIONS, in priority order. (1) Is there a SECOND REFERENCE MECHANISM anywhere beside roots.rs? Plan risk r2, and the reason the units were told to call existing verbs rather than write their own — a detector that deletes content, dereferences by hand, or duplicates GC's job is the defect this plan most feared. (2) Does removal detection distinguish ABSENT from UNREACHABLE? u-a was ruled to remove only on Ok(false), never on Err, and only after two consecutive passes — because a false reap re-buys paid enrichment for divergent content. Check the failure path, not the happy path. (3) Does search's new filtering happen BEFORE the LIMIT? Post-filtering under-fills the page and can still leak when the caller's version falls outside the fetched cap — that argument is why the store fence was granted. (4) Is the weak-match hint ADVISORY ONLY — does it change ranking, filtering, or which results return? It must not. |
| i8 | THE NO-OP BOUND (prime's rider): registering a 305-file worktree emitted 4,767 jobs of which 4,462 were enrichment jobs that stored nothing — free in provider spend, but O(files). u-a may pay that on FIRST registration and must enqueue ZERO on later passes for an unchanged worktree. There is a probe line for it. Verify the number, and verify the reconcile cadence default (30s) has its reasoning in the doc comment rather than being a number nobody chose. |
| i9 | TEST-QUALITY CHECK, and it caught a phantom finding in phase 1: search scores carry float jitter across identical calls (0.7730240968 vs 0.7730564295, same query, same hits, same order). Any assertion comparing raw scores is flaky by construction. Assertions must compare result identity (address/path/name/kind/span) or rank order. Flag every score comparison you find. Related: the weak-match floor is 0.50, calibrated against a table of should-match (0.5986-0.6985) and should-not (0.2214-0.3118) queries plus the PM's cases (noise max 0.4644, relevant min 0.5509). Judge whether the table is recorded WITH the constant, so the next person re-runs rather than re-derives. |
| i10 | MUTATION-CHECKED FIXES (this repo's rule): a test that proves a fix must FAIL without the fix. For the two headline behaviours — a worktree becoming searchable without a manual add, and a caller not being served another checkout's version — say explicitly whether the tests would catch the regression, or whether they would pass against the old code too. |
| i11 | WHAT IS OUT OF SCOPE, so you do not report it as a gap: diff-scoped scanning (ruled out on P2a evidence — identical content already costs zero), a default result cap (already exists at search.rs:141), and the question-shape hint (moved to w-agentic-query so it ships with the ask verb). Each was ruled with evidence; if you think a ruling was WRONG, say so as a finding with the counter-evidence rather than re-opening it as an omission. |
| i12 | LSP CAVEAT, binding (fleet ruling 2026-08-28): you are a fresh spawn, so rust-analyzer auto-detects and LSP-first applies to you — use go-to-definition, find-references and symbols for navigation, and expect it to work. But OMP diagnostics can FALSE-NEGATIVE: a deliberate Rust E0425 returned OK with empty items while cargo check caught it (upstream defect, filed). So LSP is for NAVIGATION; COMPILE TRUTH stays with cargo check and the gate. NEVER cite empty LSP diagnostics as evidence that code compiles. Note also that both coders worked WITHOUT LSP (it was absent fleet-wide while they built) and traced references by exact-identifier sweep, which they disclosed — so cross-crate callsite coverage is the place where their tooling was weakest and your find-references is strongest. |
| i13 | WHAT FIRST LIGHT PROVED AND WHAT IT DID NOT — read this before judging the ACs, because the receipt in the plan folder is deliberately partial. Composed run 20260828T035625Z on a private database with FAKE providers: p1_auto_discovered 0-&gt;1, p1_unchanged_reconcile_jobs=0, p4_root_still_registered 1-&gt;0, p4_deleted_content_still_served 1-&gt;0, p4_served_after_gc=0, p3_get_context_sensitive=1. Live behaviour observed: ONE root registered by hand, TWENTY auto-registered by the detector, ~15k jobs drained, zero spend. The P3 predicates are NOT proven by that run and the harness now says so rather than emitting a zero — a fake embedder makes retrieval meaningless (a query quoting the marker's own body verbatim scored 0.1889 against unrelated files). u-c's proof is therefore its own suites, which I re-ran independently on the composed tree: fs3-store pg_first_light 17/17 and fs3-daemon first_light 14/14. The live P3 measurement happens AFTER merge, as the go-live record. Judge ac-0003 on that basis and say plainly if you think it is insufficient. |
